episode.title: Add an architecture-specific Windows release artifact across build, packaging, and publication
episode.before: At first parent ac75abee43cc2b3ebbaf616b98a5c5a9c51b804d, the release builder's default target matrix contained macOS ARM64/x64, Linux ARM64/x64, and Windows x64. Only Windows x64 received a .exe name, the win32_x64 koffi native module, ZIP packaging, ZIP extraction, and release upload. The CI workflow used Bun 1.2.20.
episode.after: At pinned merge 93708de65d34ecceb2b86f626d18c2df356bd70c, the default matrix also builds Windows ARM64 using Bun 1.3.10, installs its clipboard and image native dependencies, emits pi.exe, selects and copies koffi's win32_arm64 module, creates and extracts pi-windows-arm64.zip, and includes that archive in both release creation and fallback upload. A remaining inconsistency prevents explicitly selecting windows-arm64 through --platform because the validation case still accepts only windows-x64 while its error message lists both.
episode.diff: The merge changes two files with 21 insertions and 11 deletions. scripts/build-binaries.sh adds the ARM64 target, dependencies, directory, and artifact documentation; generalizes four Windows-specific branches from an x64 equality check to the Windows platform family; maps the target architecture to the correct native-module directory; and retains ZIP packaging for Windows. .github/workflows/build-binaries.yml upgrades Bun from 1.2.20 to 1.3.10 and adds the new ZIP to release create/upload commands. No test file changed and no successful CI or runtime result is present in the evidence bundle.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge resolves PR 4458 as “Add Windows ARM64 Binary Output” and changes only the binary build script and release workflow relative to its first parent.
The first-parent builder supported five default targets and applied executable naming, koffi copying, ZIP creation, and ZIP extraction only when the target equaled windows-x64.
The change adds Windows ARM64 native clipboard and image dependencies, an output directory, and the target to the default platform matrix.
evidence_units.source: git diff ac75abee43cc2b3ebbaf616b98a5c5a9c51b804d 93708de65d34ecceb2b86f626d18c2df356bd70c -- scripts/build-binaries.sh; resulting lines 62-104

evidence_units.claim: All Windows-family targets now compile to pi.exe and are packaged as ZIP files; the koffi directory is selected as win32_arm64 for Windows ARM64 and win32_x64 otherwise.
The packaged koffi module is consumed only on Windows to enable virtual-terminal input; failure to load it is caught and degrades modified-key handling rather than terminating the application.
evidence_units.source: git show 93708de65d34ecceb2b86f626d18c2df356bd70c:packages/tui/src/terminal.ts, Terminal.start and enableWindowsVTInput methods, approximately lines 90-230

evidence_units.claim: After creating every archive, the build script deletes its staging directory and extracts the archive again, providing a structural archive-readability check but not executing the target binary.
The release workflow invokes the full build script and supplies pi-windows-arm64.zip to both release creation and fallback upload with clobber behavior.
The CI toolchain is upgraded from Bun 1.2.20 to 1.3.10; the feature-branch commit describes 1.3.10 as the minimum required version for Windows ARM.
No test file changed in the pinned merge, and the evidence bundle records no observed test-file change or status-check result.
evidence_units.source: git diff --name-only ac75abee43cc2b3ebbaf616b98a5c5a9c51b804d 93708de65d34ecceb2b86f626d18c2df356bd70c; issue-bundle.json manifest_metadata.provenance.verification and PR metadata_unavailable

evidence_units.claim: The explicit platform validator still accepts windows-x64 but not windows-arm64, although the help and error text advertise windows-arm64; therefore the new target is reached by the default all-platform build but rejected by --platform windows-arm64.

candidate_atomics.name: extend-release-target-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Extend the release target contract and prerequisites
candidate_atomics.description: Add a new architecture target consistently to the default build matrix, output layout, architecture-specific dependency installation, and minimum compiler/runtime version.

semantic_action.intent: Make the release builder capable of compiling the newly supported operating-system and architecture pair with its required native dependencies.
semantic_action.pre_state: The build matrix and installed native dependencies cover the operating system only for another architecture, and the configured compiler version predates support for the new target.
semantic_action.post_state: The default build matrix allocates the new target, installs its architecture-specific dependencies, and runs on a compiler version identified as supporting that target.
semantic_action.validation: Run the unfiltered release builder and verify it reaches the new target without a missing target, compiler, dependency, or output-directory failure. Explicit single-target validation remains unresolved for this episode.

candidate_atomics.name: package-platform-native-payload
candidate_atomics.title: Package the correct native payload for each architecture
candidate_atomics.description: Generalize operating-system packaging behavior while retaining an explicit architecture-to-native-module mapping.

semantic_action.intent: Produce an archive whose executable naming, format, and native runtime payload match the target platform and architecture.
semantic_action.pre_state: Packaging logic recognizes only one architecture as belonging to the operating-system family and hardcodes that architecture's native-module directory.
semantic_action.post_state: Every target in the operating-system family receives the family-specific executable and archive format, while each architecture receives its matching native module.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the staged archive for the family-specific executable and the native module under the architecture-selected directory, then successfully extract the archive using the family-specific extraction path.

candidate_atomics.name: publish-complete-release-artifact-set
candidate_atomics.title: Publish the new artifact in every release path
candidate_atomics.description: Add the generated architecture artifact to both initial release creation and existing-release replacement paths.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure users can obtain the newly built target artifact from the release distribution surface.
semantic_action.pre_state: The build can produce or is being extended to produce an artifact that is absent from the release creation and fallback upload lists.
semantic_action.post_state: The artifact is named in both release creation and fallback replacement commands.
semantic_action.validation: For a release tag, verify that either creation succeeds with the artifact or the fallback upload replaces it, and that the release exposes the expected artifact name.

candidate_workflows.name: add-architecture-release-artifact-end-to-end
candidate_workflows.title: Add a new architecture to a cross-platform binary release
candidate_workflows.description: Extend an existing operating-system release target to another architecture by aligning toolchain support, dependencies, platform-family packaging, architecture-specific native payloads, archive validation, and publication.

workflow_graph.goal: A full release build produces an architecture-correct archive for the new target and makes it available through every release publication path.
when_to_use: A supported operating-system family lacks a release artifact for one hardware architecture.
The binary includes optional or external native components whose packaged payload must match the target architecture.
Release publication enumerates artifact filenames explicitly.
anti_goals: Do not embed every platform's native modules into every compiled binary.
Do not change archive conventions for already-supported operating-system families without a separate requirement.
Do not treat artifact generation alone as completion when release upload lists are explicit.
Do not claim runtime compatibility from archive extraction alone.
not_applicable_when: The deliverable is architecture-neutral and has no target-specific compiler, dependency, native payload, or artifact naming requirements.
Artifacts are generated and discovered dynamically from a single authoritative target manifest without platform-specific packaging branches.
The compiler or required native dependencies do not support the requested target.
inputs: Existing target matrix and platform-family packaging rules
Release creation and fallback upload paths
workflow_graph.entry_state: A release pipeline produces artifacts for the operating-system family on at least one architecture, but the requested architecture is absent from one or more of compilation, native dependency staging, packaging, validation, or publication.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The default release build selects the new architecture, compiles it with supported tooling, stages matching native payloads, creates and re-extracts the expected archive, and includes that archive in both release creation and fallback upload; any unsupported explicit-selection path is recorded rather than hidden.

steps.condition: The requested platform/architecture is supported by the compiler and required native packages.
steps.validation: The default matrix contains the target, its staging directory and native dependencies exist, and CI selects a compiler version that supports it.

steps.condition: The target belongs to a platform family with distinct executable, archive, or native-module rules.
steps.validation: The built archive uses the platform-family executable and archive conventions, contains the architecture-matched native module, and can be extracted.

steps.condition: Release creation or update enumerates artifact names explicitly.
steps.validation: Both initial creation and fallback upload reference the exact generated artifact filename.

validation_ladder: Static contract check: the target, dependencies, staging directory, compiler target, native-module mapping, archive name, and publication name agree.
Build check: the full default target matrix completes the new target using the required compiler version.
Package check: the archive contains the family-specific executable and architecture-specific native payload.
Structural check: delete the staging directory and successfully extract the produced archive.
Publication check: verify the release exposes the expected artifact after either creation or fallback upload.
Runtime check, deferred in this episode: execute the artifact on the target architecture and exercise functionality that loads the packaged native module.
stop_conditions: Stop if the compiler does not support the target at the pinned toolchain version and no reviewed upgrade is available.
Stop if required architecture-specific dependencies or native modules cannot be resolved.
Stop if the produced artifact name differs from the name consumed by release publication.
Do not declare complete runtime support when only static inspection or archive extraction has been observed.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned implementation does not admit windows-arm64 through explicit --platform selection even though it advertises that value; default all-platform builds do include it.
No test file, CI status, build log, released asset listing, or target-machine execution result is available.
Archive extraction validates structure only; execution and native-module loading on Windows ARM64 are deferred.

unresolved_questions: Did PR 4458 pass an actual Windows ARM64 build and target-machine smoke test? PR status checks are unavailable.

Was omission of windows-arm64 from the explicit --platform validation case intentional or an implementation defect? The surrounding documentation and default matrix indicate a defect, but no review discussion is available.
Did release publication at or after the pinned commit expose a usable pi-windows-arm64.zip? No release asset evidence is included.
